view: From the sea about 1.4 km off the Platja del Centre (41.6344 N, 2.7674 E), looking west-north-west (bearing 303°) at the old town with a long lens. Sant Nicolau de Bari, 'la Catedral de la Costa', rises above the old-town roofs, seen side-on from the south-east: the nave roofs, the octagonal crossing cimbori with its low dome, and the facade crown with its pinnacles at the west end. Its 34.8 m bell tower stands at the north-west corner: two octagonal stages and a belfry with pointed arches, alternately open and blind, under a very low dome. Just to the right, about 250 m further inland, the pine-covered Parc del Castell hill rises behind the church. On its summit stands the Torre del Castell ('la Torreta'), a squat round tower about 5.8 m wide with brick merlons and the mirador railing, its foot among the pines. Around them are the old-town houses climbing the hill's foot, the seafront with its palms, the Montnegre ridge and the Turó de Montagut hills behind, and the sea glint in front. The town-landmark tier is used: the bell tower is about 48 dp to its dome (51 dp with the cross) at HERO_SCALE=1. One pinhole camera is used for the church, the castle and the hill: 1 m = 1.38 dp at the church and 1.26 dp at the castle, with positions from OpenStreetMap footprints. Hill heights come from SRTM 30 m. The ridges are ray-cast from the EU-DEM 25 m model and drawn at 0.11 of their angular height so they stay under the clock text. The church and the Torreta are floodlit at night.
